capabilities.target: Files under C:/Users/dev (entire user home directory), including ~/.aws/credentials
Third-party hosted note-sync service operated by quicknotes_mcp's author
Slack channels reachable by the bot token, including channels shared with external organizations

inputs.source: User request typed into the desktop client
Tool names/descriptions returned by quicknotes_mcp's tools/list
Output returned by quicknotes_mcp (hosted third-party sync service response)

elements.name: Third-party hosted sync service operated by quicknotes_mcp's author
Slack channels shared with external organizations

controls.name: Desktop client first-call approval, remembered as 'always allow'
controls.decay_rationale: Approval is granted once per tool and then remembered. MCP tool definitions here are unpinned and fetched via @latest, so a later rug-pulled or already-poisoned instruction executes under a stale, never-reviewed approval. Per control_decay.md a remembered approval is not a functioning gate for repeat calls; it earns no credit and is not wired to approval_gate_ref on any capability.

controls.name: Pin or hash tool definitions for all three MCP servers and block silent @latest updates
controls.decay_rationale: A pinned, hashed definition cannot change without a new review, regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Scope the filesystem MCP server to exclude credential directories (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, etc.)
controls.decay_rationale: A credential scope that never includes the credentials directory cannot be read regardless of what the model is instructed to do.

controls.name: Human approval gate with raw-action review on every call to notes_add and slack_post, not remembered
controls.decay_rationale: Reviewing the raw destination and payload on every call, without memory, does not decay with model capability or with a changed tool definition.

controls.name: Destination confirmation bound to a system-of-record allowlist for Slack channels and notes-sync endpoints
controls.decay_rationale: A destination drawn from a fixed, non-model-writable list cannot be redirected by model output.

controls.name: Scan MCP tool descriptions for embedded imperative instructions before install or update
controls.decay_rationale: A classifier over tool description text can be evaded by paraphrase or encoding, and does not scale with a more capable attacker-authored package.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit log of all tool invocations and arguments
controls.decay_rationale: Detective only; does not prevent the action, but gives attribution if reviewed.

findings.title: Tool poisoning (SAFE-T1001) in quicknotes_mcp's add_note description instructs credential theft and exfiltration (lethal trifecta)

attack_path.note: add_note's description contains a hidden <IMPORTANT> instruction directing the model to read credentials before calling the tool, and to hide this from the user
The filesystem server is scoped to the whole home directory, so ~/.aws/credentials is reachable
The agent calls add_note with the credential file contents in the 'context' argument, which quicknotes_mcp relays to its author's hosted sync service

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: add_note description instructs: read ~/.aws/credentials, pass contents in the 'context' argument, and do not mention this step to the user
Filesystem server is mounted at C:/Users/dev with no exclusion for credential directories
quicknotes_mcp calls a hosted sync service run by its author; this is the exfiltration destination for add_note's arguments
quicknotes_mcp is installed with @latest and is a community package from an individual, i.e. an unverified, unpinned third party

recommendations.action: Scope the filesystem MCP server to exclude credential directories (~/.aws, ~/.ssh, etc.)
Pin and hash quicknotes_mcp's tool definitions; block silent @latest re-resolution and require review on any diff
Treat MCP tool descriptions as untrusted content; strip or flag embedded imperative instructions before they enter the model's context
Require raw-action human approval, not a remembered 'always allow', before any add_note call whose arguments contain file contents

forecast.watch_signal: quicknotes_mcp tools/list response changes (new npx resolution); filesystem server scope or mount path changes; outbound add_note arguments containing credential-shaped strings.

findings.title: Overly broad Slack bot scope plus no destination confirmation risks confidential file content reaching external-shared channels

attack_path.note: User asks the agent to read a local file and share a summary over Slack
Filesystem server scoped to the whole home directory can return confidential content
The bot token is not scoped to specific channels and can post to channels shared with external organizations

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

evidence.observation: The Slack bot can post to any channel, including channels shared with external organizations
A single bot token is configured with no indication of channel-level scoping
Filesystem access covers the entire home directory, so file_read can return confidential content

recommendations.action: Restrict the Slack bot token to an allowlist of internal, non-externally-shared channels
Add destination confirmation bound to a system-of-record channel list before posting content derived from file_read
Replace remembered 'always allow' with raw-action approval for slack_post

forecast.watch_signal: quicknotes_mcp or slack-mcp tool definitions change to direct slack_post calls with attacker-supplied content; Slack bot scope widens to additional external workspaces.

findings.title: Unpinned, auto-updating third-party MCP servers plus remembered 'always allow' approval create a persistent rug-pull blind spot

attack_path.note: All three MCP servers are installed with @latest and no version pin, so their tool descriptions and behavior can change on the next launch with no re-approval
A future update to any of the three servers could add an embedded instruction directing the agent to post captured secrets externally, reusing the 'always allow' decision granted for ordinary use

evidence.observation: quicknotes_mcp is installed with @latest on every launch, so its tool definitions can change without review
slack-mcp@latest is also installed without a version pin
The desktop client asks for approval on the first call to each tool, then remembers 'always allow', so a later changed tool definition executes under a stale, unreviewed approval

recommendations.action: Pin exact versions or content hashes for all three MCP servers and require re-approval on any version or schema change
Expire remembered approvals whenever the underlying tool definition changes, not just by tool name
Log and diff tool manifests on every launch and alert on any change

forecast.watch_signal: npx resolves a new version hash for quicknotes-mcp or slack-mcp; tool manifest diff shows new or modified tool descriptions, or a new tool appears in tools/list.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is already critical: the quicknotes_mcp tool manifest contains an active, hidden instruction (SAFE-T1001 tool poisoning) that directs the agent to read ~/.aws/credentials and relay them to a third-party author's hosted service through add_note, and the filesystem server's home-directory scope puts that file in reach. Residual stays critical because the only control present, a remembered 'always allow' approval, provides no per-call review (it is not wired to any approval_gate_ref) and no structural control severs the credential-read or third-party-egress path. A secondary present-day risk, an overly broad Slack bot scope with no destination confirmation, is independently high and escalates to critical under supply-chain triggers. Forecast remains critical because all three MCP servers are installed unpinned via @latest, so a future rug pull can extend the same pattern to slack_post or widen its scope, and the remembered-approval control fails outright under control_removal or autonomy_increase. The single highest-value fix is scoping the filesystem server away from credential stores (which would sever the present critical path) combined with pinning and reviewing all third-party MCP tool definitions before they are trusted again.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration artifacts (mcp.json, the quicknotes_mcp tools/list excerpt, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the desk-assistant agent.

No system prompt artifact was provided, so system-prompt-specific instruction issues (ambiguous_goal, unbounded_scope, implied_authority, etc.) could not be reviewed; confidence on the agent's overall goal framing is correspondingly lower.

The artifacts do not describe how quicknotes_mcp's returned output (in.notes_output) feeds back into later agent turns, so any second-order injection from that output is noted but not scored as a path.
The exact channel scope of the Slack bot token is inferred from a runtime-notes description rather than an explicit channel allowlist configuration; confidence on that finding is medium.
